questions.sampleAnswer: Crediting sources of data is important as it allows the researcher to show evidence of their results and research findings. A researcher can credit data sources through the construction of a bibliography which provides references of the secondary research articles, while maintaining integrity and preventing plagiarism. An appendix can include articles and data sources used in the research process to enhance authenticity.

questions.sampleAnswer: Through completing a literature review, the researcher is exposed to and engages with a range of secondary sources about their topic. This allows the researcher to deepen their knowledge and understanding of their topic which gives them more insight when analysing their results. questions.sampleAnswer: Individuals from rural and remote families may have a lower socioeconomic status during times of drought, flood, or unproductive farming periods. During this time of hardship, finances may be quite low affecting individual’s ability to access high fee health services such as dental, specialist doctor appointments or private health insurance. During such times an individual may neglect to use any of these services due to their expensive nature, possibly leading to further chronic health conditions. A person with a physical disability in a rural or remote area may have a reduced choice of specialised health services and may have to travel long distances to access physiotherapy or rehabilitation. This extended travel time will be expensive and tiresome for the person as it may require specialist transport services or a support person.

questions.sampleAnswer: Both foster and stepparents are legally unable to make major health and medical decisions on behalf of a dependant, for example, electing to receive vaccinations. The legal constraints can affect the social parents’ decision-making authority, potentially causing stress and frustration, affecting their emotional wellbeing. The stepparent may have a deep emotional connection, therefore, not being able to make major medical or health decisions may leave them feeling frustrated and helpless. Having this additional complication can affect their emotional wellbeing as they may feel ‘less’ of a parent if they are unable to make these important decisions. Foster parents often have limited information on a child’s medical history. They can experience conflict with biological parents in relation to health and medical decisions, this conflict can cause stress, affecting their physical wellbeing.

criteria.text: Provides a thorough explanation of how appropriate sampling can assist a researcher in achieving validity and reliability

Demonstrates some understanding of sampling processes and/or validity and/or reliability
Provides some relevant information

questions.sampleAnswer: A researcher should carefully select a sample representing a subset of the population to ensure valid and reliable data is collected. For example, to ensure validity, when conducting research about primary school aged children in NSW, it would be essential to ensure that the students researched are of primary school age. A researcher should consider their sample size to ensure the total number of participants will accurately represent the total population. A large sample size ensures reliability so if the research was repeated it would provide similar results. A researcher could apply a stratified random sample method to allow the researcher to organise their sample population into categories eg city, regional and remote. The researcher would then select a similar number of individuals to research across the different categories, further enhancing reliability and validity of the research.

questions.sampleAnswer: Employees may choose to access a variety of patterns of work following a change in family circumstances such as the birth of a child. A person may choose to access part-time or casual work rather than full-time when beginning to re-enter the workforce following a period of parental leave. A part-time work pattern would be effective in allowing an individual to fulfil their parenting responsibilities, yet still being able to work on certain days of the week. Shift work would also be very effective in allowing a couple to care for a dependant who suddenly needed constant care. Each person would be able to work different shifts and fulfil the caring obligation when they arrived home. This would be effective as the dependant would receive the care required and both workers would be able to earn a living to support the family.

answersCouldInclude: Workplace structures can influence the efficiency of a workplace, through happier and more productive employees that feel supported and valued.
Workplace culture initiatives
Prayer room – Allows for staff to have their faith and prayer obligations met. Workers can use this room without having to go offsite saving time, allowing the worker to be more productive.

Staff kitchen – Workers can store food and or gather socially at lunch. Workers may feel supported and valued as well as not having to waste time buying food and making long trips away from the workplace.

Childcare – Allows workers to utilise in-house childcare centres. They can bring their child to work saving travel time. This would increase workplace efficiency as workers would not have to leave earlier to pick up children and work more productively knowing their children are being cared for close by.
Flexible work patterns and practices

Flexible work arrangements – Workers may be able to negotiate with their employer staggered start and finish times. This allows workers to drop off / pick up children from childcare. Workers with this arrangement would feel valued and work more productively knowing that their needs are catered for, further enhancing workplace efficiency.
Legislation

Workplace, health and safety laws – Maintain stringent safety in and around the workplace environment. Employers and employees are obligated to report and respond to immediate threats to safety. The laws increase worker efficiency as workers are confident that their safety needs are upheld and are more likely to work efficiently without fear of injury, disability or death.
